epinephrines, phenylephrines and methoxamines induce cutaneous anesthesia via α1A-, α1B- and α1D- adrenoceptors in rats.
epinephrinedriven local anesthesia in the skin of rats is mediated by α1A-, α1B- and α1D-adrenergic receptors.
epinephine, phenylephine, and methoxanine act via α1-adrenoreceptors to induce cutaneaous anesthesia in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of local anesthesia of epinephrin, phenylephrin and methoxamin in rat.
the mechanism of action of adrenoceptor agonist-induced cutaneous anesthesia in conscious, un-anesthetized rats.
the local anesthetic activity of epinephrin, L-phenyl-ephrine, and methoxamin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cutaneous anesthesia induced via adrenoceptor agonism in the skin is a result of the activation of α1-adrenergic receptors.
epinephrines, phenylephrines, and methoxamines all act via α1-adrenergic receptors to exert their local anesthesia activity.
epinephine, phenylephine and methoxamine are all potent cutaneous local anesthetics, which act mainly via mixed subtype of α1-adrenoreceptors in rat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cutaneous anesthesia produced by epinephrines, phenylephrines, and methoxamines is mediated by α1-adrenergic receptors.
the cutaneous anesthesia induced from epinephrine and phenylephrine is mainly mediated by α1-adrenergic receptor subtypes, and methoxamines by α1-adrenoreceptors.

The main takeaway from our work is that
epinephrines and phenylephrines are potent local anesthetics that act via the α1-adrenocepter.
α1-adrenocepto rs are the major targets for epinephrine and its analogs in producing local anesthesia.
